subject.title: refactor(qa): migrate Matrix scenarios into QA Lab

question: Should this stack own both the Matrix QA dependency/runtime migration and the process-wide Gateway admission change, and should the dependency graph be authorized for head 6e962a55f9f7572ef33b508189e7b09986aea4e8?
rationale: The patch is well-proven and has no remaining concrete correctness finding, but automated review cannot approve an exact-head dependency exception or decide whether an availability-sensitive core lifecycle change belongs inside this QA migration.

options.title: Approve the current architecture
options.body: Authorize the exact dependency graph and land the stack after the relevant QA and Gateway owners confirm the temporary shim and admission lifecycle contracts.

options.title: Split the Gateway change
options.body: Move the admission helper and channel-restart call-site changes into a dedicated core PR, then authorize and land the QA migration separately.

options.title: Pause the migration stack
options.body: Keep this and its dependent workflow PR open until maintainers choose a different permanent ownership boundary for Matrix QA.

recommendation.title: Approve the current architecture
recommendation.body: Authorize the exact dependency graph and land the stack after the relevant QA and Gateway owners confirm the temporary shim and admission lifecycle contracts.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the active Matrix QA consolidation stack and are best positioned to coordinate the required QA, dependency, and Gateway owner decisions.
